newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures slip more late, most end down.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures slip more late, most end down.

text.p: IMM currency futures slipped again in light late trading Friday, with most units ending lower.

September marks nearly returned again late to the contract low at $0.5453 set overnight, while Swiss francs, sterling and Canadian dollar also attracted some closing sales that pressured them back toward the session's price troughs.

But brokers said afternoon action stayed spotty, with turnover concentrated during the morning. Price boards showed estimated volume in September marks, yen, Swiss, and Canadian dollar at 15,000, 14,000, 11,000 and 5,000, respectively.
Turnover swelled in the Mexican peso, however, where daily volume totalled roughly 7,000 contracts, brokers added.

They said the Mexican currency futures rallied on technical buying that also sparked shortcovering as shorts, including some big institutions, who had looked for the peso to erode, bailed out instead.
"It was just technical buying," said one bank floor broker of the peso's rise. "It looked like spot was going to go 7.7900 or 7.8000 (pesos per U.S. dollar). It isn't. It's going the other way."
Brokers also said little had changed in their perceptions of the U.S. dollar, which they still viewed as easily heading higher unless fundamentals change drastically.
"I think most people think that this is the real dollar deal -- be long bonds, long dollars and long stocks," added the bank broker. "It (dollar) does look pretty good."
He said some pundits forecast a rise in the U.S. unit to 1.88 marks, or roughly $0.5338 basis September futures.
Similarly, some brokers said the dollar's rise above 116.00 yen had soured the yen's technical picture again, as nearby futures tested support at $0.008607 or 117.00 cash.
The brokers said a dollar rise toward 118.00 was not out of the question. Such a move would shove nearby yen futures toward $0.008536.

At settlement, September yen lost $0.000069 to $0.008608, marks eased $0.0012 to $0.5456, Swiss francs declined $0.0036 to $0.6630, sterling dropped $0.0096 to $1.6612, Canadian dollar lost $0.0022 to $0.7238, Aussie dollar rose $0.0010 to $0.7388, and Mexican peso rose $0.000400 to $0.125975.
